why: Drops sidestepAroundBlockage's own mine-refusal guard, the constraint its doc comment claims mirrors dangerAvoidMove's two-perpendicular passes -- a dodge that solves the shell by walking onto a mine. No existing test reached this specific line before this PR's re-pin work: the two-perpendicular tests (danger.test.ts's 'picks the dodge side that does not step toward a nearby armed mine') never reach sidestepAroundBlockage at all (a wall-clear perpendicular returns before it is called), and the pre-existing 'sidesteps onto a navigable heading' fixture carries no mine. Closed here by 'refuses a sidestep candidate that steps toward an armed mine': a corridor where the wheel's only two navigable candidates (due east/west) tie at the worst possible lateral-clearance score, with an armed mine placed on the tie-winning (east) side. Measured directly by disambiguating this line's two occurrences with the full three-line context above (the guard also appears verbatim in dangerAvoidMove's own two-perpendicular loop) -- the `find` string is unique to this function because only here is it immediately followed by the lateral-clearance score line.
killedBy: dodging near walls (issue #224) refuses a sidestep candidate that steps toward an armed mine
